title: Metabolic encephalopathy and systemic disease neurology

steps.tx: **Wernicke encephalopathy** results from acute **thiamine** (vitamin B1) deficiency, classically presenting with the clinical triad of acute encephalopathy, oculomotor dysfunction with horizontal and vertical nystagmus or abducens palsy, and prominent gait ataxia. High-dose parenteral thiamine replacement must always precede glucose administration to prevent precipitating sudden, irreversible metabolic decompensation.
steps.say: Wernicke encephalopathy results from acute thiamine vitamin B1 deficiency classically presenting with the clinical triad of acute encephalopathy oculomotor dysfunction with horizontal and vertical nystagmus or abducens palsy and prominent gait ataxia. High-dose parenteral thiamine replacement must always precede glucose administration to prevent precipitating sudden irreversible metabolic decompensation.

vis.alt: MRI showing bilateral mammillary body, medial thalamic, and periaqueductal hyperintensities in Wernicke encephalopathy.
vis.caption: Periaqueductal and mammillary body lesions in Wernicke encephalopathy (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Characteristic magnetic resonance imaging findings in acute **Wernicke encephalopathy** demonstrate symmetrical hyperintensity and enhancement of the **mammillary bodies**, medial thalami, periaqueductal gray matter, and tectum on T2 and FLAIR acquisitions. Prompt recognition prevents permanent anterograde memory impairment and chronic confabulation characteristic of Korsakoff syndrome.
steps.say: Characteristic magnetic resonance imaging findings in acute Wernicke encephalopathy demonstrate symmetrical hyperintensity and enhancement of the mammillary bodies medial thalami periaqueductal gray matter and tectum on T2 and FLAIR acquisitions. Prompt recognition prevents permanent anterograde memory impairment and chronic confabulation characteristic of Korsakoff syndrome.

left.title: Typical Neuroimaging Sites
points: Mammillary bodies atrophy and contrast enhancement
Dorsomedial thalamic nuclei symmetric T2 hyperintensity
Periaqueductal gray matter and tectal plate
Floor of the fourth ventricle and area postrema

right.title: Atypical / Cortical Sites
points: Cerebral cortex and peri-Rolandic sulci
Caudate nuclei and putamen hyperintensities
Cerebellar vermis and dentate nuclei
More prevalent in non-alcoholic thiamine deficiency

steps.tx: **Osmotic demyelination syndrome**, historically known as central pontine myelinolysis, is caused by overly rapid correction of severe chronic **hyponatremia** exceeding **10-12** mEq/L per **24** hours, causing spastic quadriparesis, pseudobulbar palsy, and locked-in syndrome due to extensive pontine oligodendrocyte dehydration across vulnerable pathways.
steps.say: Osmotic demyelination syndrome historically known as central pontine myelinolysis is caused by overly rapid correction of severe chronic hyponatremia exceeding 10-12 mEq/L per 24 hours causing spastic quadriparesis pseudobulbar palsy and locked-in syndrome due to extensive pontine oligodendrocyte dehydration across vulnerable pathways.

left.title: Pathogenesis & Risk
points: Chronic hyponatremia (>48 hours duration)
Brain adaptation via loss of organic osmolytes
Rapid hypertonic sodium correction >10-12 mEq/L/day
High risk in alcoholism, malnutrition, liver failure

right.title: Clinical Manifestations
points: Delayed presentation 2 to 6 days after correction
Spastic quadriparesis and pseudobulbar palsy
Classic locked-in syndrome with preserved blinking
Trident-shaped pontine hyperintensity on MRI

steps.tx: **Hepatic encephalopathy** is characterized by elevated blood ammonia, asterixis or flapping tremor, and bilateral symmetrical frontally predominant **triphasic waves** on electroencephalography. Astrocytic glutamine accumulation increases intracellular osmolarity, inducing low-grade cerebral oedema, impaired neurotransmission, asterixis, and progressive fluctuating cognitive dysfunction in patients with hepatic failure.
steps.say: Hepatic encephalopathy is characterized by elevated blood ammonia asterixis or flapping tremor and bilateral symmetrical frontally predominant triphasic waves on electroencephalography. Astrocytic glutamine accumulation increases intracellular osmolarity inducing low-grade cerebral oedema impaired neurotransmission asterixis and progressive fluctuating cognitive dysfunction in patients with hepatic failure.

rows: Comatose state unresponsive to verbal cues
Severe delta activity and burst suppression

steps.tx: **Subacute combined degeneration** of the spinal cord is caused by **vitamin B12** or cobalamin deficiency, producing demyelination of the posterior and lateral columns manifesting with sensory ataxia, spasticity, and absent ankle jerks with extensor plantars, creating a classical inverted plantar reflex dissociation.
steps.say: Subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord is caused by vitamin B12 or cobalamin deficiency producing demyelination of the posterior and lateral columns manifesting with sensory ataxia spasticity and absent ankle jerks with extensor plantars creating a classical inverted plantar reflex dissociation.

left.title: Posterior Column Deficits
points: Loss of vibration and proprioception
Sensory ataxia and positive Romberg sign
Lhermitte sign on neck flexion
Inverted V sign on spinal T2 MRI

right.title: Lateral Column Deficits
points: Spastic paraparesis and hyperreflexia
Extensor plantar responses (Babinski sign)
Absent ankle jerks due to peripheral neuropathy
Characteristic upper and lower motor sign mix

steps.tx: **Uremic encephalopathy** presents with fluctuating mental status, multifocal **myoclonus**, asterixis, and prominent seizure susceptibility, improving rapidly following adequate hemodialysis. Organic acids and guanidino neurotoxins accumulate systemically, inhibiting central GABAergic neurotransmission and increasing cortical irritability throughout both cerebral hemispheres in severe renal failure.
steps.say: Uremic encephalopathy presents with fluctuating mental status multifocal myoclonus asterixis and prominent seizure susceptibility improving rapidly following adequate hemodialysis. Organic acids and guanidino neurotoxins accumulate systemically inhibiting central GABAergic neurotransmission and increasing cortical irritability throughout both cerebral hemispheres in severe renal failure.

left.title: Clinical Hallmarks
points: Fluctuating delirium, apathy, and cognitive clouding
Multifocal myoclonus and prominent asterixis
Elevated seizure susceptibility and tremors
Associated with high blood urea nitrogen and creatinine

right.title: Management & Pitfalls
points: Prompt initiation of hemodialysis clears neurotoxins
Rapid symptom resolution following metabolic clearance
Dialysis disequilibrium syndrome from rapid urea shifts
Avoidance of neurotoxic drug accumulation in renal failure

steps.tx: **Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome** manifests with acute headache, altered mental status, visual disturbances, and **vasogenic** subcortical edema predominantly affecting the parieto-occipital white matter on magnetic resonance imaging, requiring prompt blood pressure normalization to avoid secondary cytotoxic infarction across vulnerable cerebral territories.
steps.say: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome manifests with acute headache altered mental status visual disturbances and vasogenic subcortical edema predominantly affecting the parieto-occipital white matter on magnetic resonance imaging requiring prompt blood pressure normalization to avoid secondary cytotoxic infarction across vulnerable cerebral territories.

left.title: Pathophysiological Triggers
points: Severe acute blood pressure surges exceeding autoregulation
Calcineurin inhibitor toxicity (cyclosporine, tacrolimus)
Pre-eclampsia and eclampsia in obstetric patients
Autoimmune vasculopathies and high-dose chemotherapy

right.title: Neuroimaging Hallmarks
points: Symmetric cortical and subcortical vasogenic oedema
Predilection for bilateral parieto-occipital lobes
Hyperintensity on T2/FLAIR with elevated ADC values
Complete reversibility upon prompt blood pressure control

steps.tx: **Copper deficiency** myeloneuropathy causes an identical clinical syndrome to vitamin B12 deficiency (**subacute combined degeneration**) and is frequently associated with high dietary zinc ingestion or previous gastric bypass surgery. Copper supplementation prevents neurological progression and treats concurrent microcytic or sideroblastic anaemia.
